findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up in fish fry station. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: During the inspection, the bleach sanitizer spray at the main bar area was tested and recorded at a concentration over 200ppm. This bleach sanitizer spray bottle was pulled from service and had water added to reduce the concentration to 200ppm.Ensure test strips are used during each service to ensure the sanitizer concentration meets the proper concentration. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The chemical sanitizer spray bottle in the fry area was tested and recorded at 0ppm. Bleach was added to this spray bottle and brought into compliance at 100ppm. The spray bottle should be tested at regular intervals to ensure the sanitizer concentration is sufficeint for sanitizing surfaces.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Workers were observed engaging in food preparation activities without first washing their hands. Workers were instructed to remove their gloves, wash their hands in the designated hand sink and then they may equip gloves. Ensure that workers properly wasn’t heir hands between tasks and before engaging in food service activities.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The sink basins in the frying building were observed to be utilized for purposes besides hand washing. With 2 sink basins, during food preparation and service, one of the sink basins need to be designated as an official hand sink in order for the workers to have access to a hand sink. Ensure a sink basin is designated with appropriate signage, soap, and disposable paper towels.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The ice scoop holder and the can opener were observed soiled at the start of the inspection. Each items was removed form service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that food contact surfaces remain clean to sight and touch. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The baffle of the ice machine is observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residues along the metal fold and the edges of the baffle. Ensure this surface is properly cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: The fry building is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings along the interior walls of the back room, galley room, and main room. Fidelis is the facility PCO and should be contacted and made aware of the observations and discuss plans for eradication. A follow-up is being issued for Monday, November 7th, 2022 to observe the eradication and prevention process.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: At the start of the inspection, the tongs to utilized to remove fish from the fryers were observed stored with the contact surface in contact with a very soiled metal piece. The tongs were removed from this location and placed properly on the food basins. Ensure utensils intended for food contact are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
5-403.11: It was confirmed in the fry building that the mop water is dumped outside and not through a proper disposal system. This practice should stop and the mop water should be disposed of utilizing the public sewer. Ensure workers are educated and the effort is established to properly dispose of waste water.
5-403.11: SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Facility is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings, dead insects, and other various debris/soils in the fry room back room, galley room, and main room. Ensure that equipment is pulled away from walls and that the premise is cleaned with the removal of the droppings, insects, and various debris/soils.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
